name: Reinforced planking
blurb: Doubled planking and extra frames: a quarter more hull to lose before she leaks badly, at a fifth of a knot.

name: Improved pumps
blurb: Bigger bilge pumps: a holed hull floods half as fast, so she keeps her speed and sits higher until you can patch her.

name: Quality canvas
blurb: A new suit of close-woven cotton duck that holds its shape: 5% faster at every sail.

name: Storm sails
blurb: Heavy-weather canvas for the reefed and half sails: they carry 4 knots more wind before the rigging strains.

name: Improved blocks and rigging
blurb: Bronze-sheaved blocks and new running rigging: sail changes take 40% less time, which helps most when sailing solo.

name: Expanded hold
blurb: Bulkheads moved and the 'tween deck opened up: a quarter more cargo, sitting a little deeper and a fifth of a knot slower.

name: Hidden compartment
blurb: A false bulkhead aft of the hold: a revenue search is about half as likely to find what's behind it, for a tenth of the hold.

name: Aneroid barometer
blurb: A fine Naudet aneroid that reads small changes in the glass: the chart's forecast reaches a full day ahead instead of twelve hours.

name: Sounding machine
blurb: A Kelvin sounding machine instead of the hand lead: the depth warning sounds at three times your draft, not twice.

name: Marine telescope
blurb: A long brass telescope instead of the old spyglass: twice the magnification, and you can make out a ship's papers half again as far off.

name: Heavy anchor
blurb: A heavier bower and more chain: holds in a full gale where the old one would drag.

name: Bow swivel
blurb: A one-pounder on a pivot in the bows: chain for her rigging, grape for her deck, or a shot across her bow to make her think. The first gun a solo captain can work.

name: Light cannon, a pair
blurb: Two old four-pounders, one each side behind the bulwarks: round shot to hole a hull. A broadside needs hands to work it, so only the larger schooner carries them.

name: Rifle
blurb: A lever-action rifle and a box of cartridges: cut a tow line, put out a lamp, or pick off a man at the wheel. Precise, short-ranged and lethal.

name: Gun sights
blurb: Notched sights filed true on the guns: shots fall a quarter closer to where you aimed.

name: Bored-out barrels
blurb: The bores reamed out for a heavier charge: the guns reach a fifth further.

name: Improved carriages
blurb: Iron-trucked carriages and better tackle: the guns reload a fifth faster.

name: Hidden gun ports
blurb: Hinged bulwark panels and a tarpaulin over the swivel: a ship you come up on sees an honest trader until the guns run out. The law's description of her doesn't change.
